mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT over the next four weeks will raise weekday trips to Manhattan shops and restaurants, lifting RETAIL_REC relative to the last four weeks. The signal is strongest if both series keep rising from their current depressed levels.
evidence_refs: fact:both remain deeply negative but have risen for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: Reject if WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue rising for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not improve versus the prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL remains above its current level while WORKPLACES stays very depressed, more time spent near home will shift purchases toward local retail and delivery pickup channels, pushing RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks. This fails if home-based activity does not translate into neighborhood retail visits.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 while WORKPLACES remains below -60
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive and WORKPLACES is strongly negative in all four weeks
failure_condition: Reject if RESIDENTIAL stays above +20 and WORKPLACES stays below -60 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A further week-over-week rise in TRANSIT from its current trough should precede higher retail traffic within one week, because easier access to Manhattan commercial areas restores short discretionary trips. The effect should appear only when TRANSIT is improving rather than merely flat.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises week-on-week after being below -75
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has improved each week from -79.4 to -75.1
failure_condition: Reject if TRANSIT rises week-on-week from below -75 but RETAIL_REC is not higher in the following week.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility rebounds sharply while GROCERY_PHARM stays weak, outdoor social activity will substitute for indoor shopping trips and keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks. The mechanism requires park-driven substitution, not a broad reopening of all activities.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above -45 while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -35
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM are both still far below baseline
failure_condition: Reject if PARKS rises above -45 while GROCERY_PHARM stays below -35 and RETAIL_REC nevertheless improves over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As the late-spring shift favors outdoor mobility, a steady rise in PARKS should coincide with a gradual rebound in discretionary retail visits over the next two weeks. The seasonal channel fails if park activity rises only because indoor commerce remains closed and shopping does not follow.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -67.1 to -51.3 over three weeks
failure_condition: Reject if PARKS keeps rising for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the prior two-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, worsening TRANSIT and WORKPLACES should mechanically suppress retail footfall over the following four weeks because fewer commuters and fewer on-site workers reduce downtown shopping opportunities. The signal is strongest when both series fall together.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall by at least 5 points from their current week
evidence_refs: fact:both remain deeply negative in the snapshot
failure_condition: Reject if TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall by at least 5 points yet RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve while RETAIL_REC remains depressed, consumers are reallocating trips to essential errands rather than discretionary shopping, which keeps retail-and-recreation mobility from recovering over the next one week. The effect should show up quickly when pantry-restocking trips substitute for leisure shopping.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -35 while RETAIL_REC remains below -80
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM has improved sharply while RETAIL_REC is nearly flat
failure_condition: Reject if GROCERY_PHARM rises above -35 while RETAIL_REC remains below -80 and RETAIL_REC still rises in the next week.

mechanism_narrative: A broad mobility recovery across TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and GROCERY_PHARM indicates normalization of daily routines that should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if the gains are isolated to one series and do not reflect wider circulation.
evidence_refs: fact:all three series improved from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if at least two of TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and GROCERY_PHARM keep improving for four weeks but RETAIL_REC does not rise versus the last four weeks.
